decisions.reason: Fouling detection automation fits the firm's announced push toward digitally networked, efficient infrastructure with energy recovery, and the R&D investment, likely tied to funded research, makes management inclined to persist and attribute any slow early uptake to the long municipal procurement cycles.

A web tool for weir dimensioning builds directly on the firm's core flood-control and hydraulic engineering offer, costs little to maintain, and supports lead generation with engineering planners, so there is no reason to withdraw it after just one year.

The fouling detection system is the hardware counterpart to Product A and is publicly showcased as part of the firm's energy-efficiency direction, so management will stand by it and treat any disappointing early results as temporary market-development issues.
